fact: The Minister of Posts and Telecommunications announced on 21 January 2025 that Cameroon is developing a national AI strategy, which is under development with no adoption stated.

The Nkafu Policy Institute brief states that Cameroon launched its National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (SNIA) in July 2025, with targets to 2040 of 60,000 AI professionals, 12,000 direct AI jobs and 0.8-1.2% of GDP.

The OECD AI Policy Observatory entry, updated 28 April 2026, lists Cameroon's National AI Strategy (SNIA), run by the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications, with status 'Proposed or under development' and start year 2025, while its text says it was unveiled in July 2025.

TechAfrica News reports that the government officially launched its first National AI Strategy (SNIA), unveiled by the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications at the second CONIA consultations; the date is the article's publication date.
L'Economie reports that the national AI development strategy was unveiled by the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications at CONIA on 7-8 July 2025.
ITWeb reports Cameroon is fine-tuning its draft National Strategy for the Development of AI, discussed at national consultations in Yaounde the previous day (7 July 2025).

A law firm says that, after a public tender, the Government of Cameroon through the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications selected it to lead drafting of the National Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence, with an implementation and financing plan and a government AI roadmap.

fact: The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications issued a restricted national tender on 17 September 2024 to recruit a firm to draft Cameroon's national AI strategy and government roadmap, estimated at XAF 60 million, with a three-month execution.
Minister Minette Libom Li Likeng said the government is developing an AI development strategy, with national AI consultations held (Business in Cameroon, relaying Cameroon Tribune).
